causal_chain: Better separation of supportive versus misleading collaborative evidence improves full-sort ranking quality, especially for ambiguous and long-tail targets.
Scoring candidates with direct affinity plus excited transport minus inhibited transport raises preference-consistent items and demotes popularity-driven or mixed-taste false positives.
Splitting this residual structure into excitation and inhibition graphs gives separate collaborative evidence for 'go-together' and 'should-not-follow-from-this-history' item signals.
Train-only user histories define item-item residual relations after subtracting popularity-expected co-occurrence.
User-conditioned gating over historical items selects which signed graph paths are relevant for the current user's latent intent.
blind_projection.closest_parent: A recommender that forms each user's score through a signed residual propagation state over item-item transitions, with separate excitation and inhibition operators gated by the user's latent intent, will rank held-out items better than static interaction scoring because it can amplify coherent co-consumption evidence while actively suppressing misleading associations created by popularity and mixed-taste histories.
blind_projection.competing_explanation: Any gain could come from adding an item-item graph side channel or extra parameters rather than from the signed residual excitation/inhibition mechanism itself.
discriminative_predictions: Against a matched unsigned-transport control with the same embeddings and graph budget, the signed model should show larger NDCG@10 gains for users whose training histories span multiple popularity bands or mixed genres.
If the mechanism is real, improvement should be stronger on tail and mid-popularity held-out items than on head items dominated by direct-affinity baselines.
Randomly flipping residual-edge signs or collapsing positive/negative graphs into a single unsigned graph should reduce any benefit if signed separation is the causal mechanism.
Removing the inhibition channel while keeping excitation should increase scores for popular false positives more than for true held-out positives.
expected_evidence: Ablation to mechanism-off direct-affinity scoring loses any gains attributable to transport.
Matched-control comparison to unsigned transport isolates whether signed inhibition matters beyond generic graph smoothing.
Per-item-bucket and per-user-history-diversity slices show whether benefits concentrate where misleading co-occurrence is most plausible.
Qualification runs complete within the frozen ML-1M protocol using a candidate-local RecBole GeneralRecommender.
blind_projection.falsifier: If a parameter-matched unsigned transport control matches or exceeds the signed residual model, and inhibition ablations do not selectively worsen popular false-positive ranking, then the signed excitation/inhibition hypothesis is not supported.
blind_projection.high_change_justification: This candidate changes the core relation from user-item matching alone to signed item-item residual transport, changes the model structure by introducing dual propagation channels and user-conditioned gating, and changes the interaction structure by scoring through history-dependent graph transport rather than a static embedding match.
blind_projection.hypothesis: A pairwise-trained recommender that builds train-only signed residual item-item graphs, propagates each user's historical signal through separate excitation and inhibition channels, and gates those channels by user intent will improve ML-1M full-sort NDCG@10 over static collaborative filters and unsigned transport controls because it can amplify preference-consistent collaborative paths while subtracting misleading popularity-shaped associations.
implementation_requirements: Construct train-only sparse item-item residual matrices from timestamp-ordered user histories using popularity-corrected co-occurrence or transition residuals, then split into positive and negative parts.
Define candidate score as direct user-item affinity plus gated excitation transport score minus gated inhibition transport score.
Implement a candidate-local RecBole GeneralRecommender with pairwise training and full-sort prediction support.
Maintain user embeddings, item embeddings, and a lightweight history-attention gate that weights historical items for each user.
Precompute or efficiently apply sparse excitation and inhibition propagation to item embeddings inside PyTorch/Scipy without using held-out data.
Provide ablations for mechanism-off direct-affinity scoring and for a matched unsigned-transport control with comparable parameter count.
blind_projection.matched_control_requirement: Use the same backbone embeddings, history gate, training loss, and sparse graph construction budget, but replace the split signed residual graphs with a single unsigned normalized co-occurrence/transition graph and additive transport only; this isolates signed inhibition from generic graph augmentation.
blind_projection.mechanism_change: Introduce a dual-channel signed residual propagation scorer: build positive and negative residual item-item graphs from train histories, aggregate a user's history through both graphs with learned attention, then combine direct affinity, positive transport, and subtractive negative transport in the ranking score.
blind_projection.mechanism_off_definition: Set excitation and inhibition transport coefficients to zero and score only by direct user-item affinity with the same embeddings and pairwise training loop, leaving all graph-derived channels inactive.
blind_projection.minimal_testable_wedge: Add a train-only signed residual item-item transport module with separate positive and negative channels to a pairwise collaborative scorer, and test whether this outperforms the same scorer with graph channels removed or collapsed to unsigned transport.
blind_projection.research_question: Can an executable signed residual item-item transport mechanism, with separate excitation and inhibition channels gated by user intent, outperform static and unsigned collaborative ranking under the frozen ML-1M full-sort pairwise protocol?
blind_projection.resource_hypothesis: The candidate is feasible within the stated budget because ML-1M item cardinality permits sparse signed item-item matrices, propagation can be implemented with precomputed scipy sparse operators or sparse PyTorch multiplication, and the added trainable components are limited to embeddings, lightweight gating, and a small number of channel weights.
